before.description:
On the  Go‑Checkout  page related to the  Email  and  Confirm Email  fields. When the same email is entered but with different letter casing (e.g., uppercase in one field and lowercase in the other), the system flags it as a mismatch. 

email comparisons are case‑insensitive. It should not give error message for same email address regardless it is upper case or lower case.
before.title: Go‑Checkout Page - Email & Confirm Email Case Sensitivity

after.description: On the Go-Checkout page, the Email and Confirm Email fields are compared case-sensitively, so entering the same address with different letter casing (e.g. Name@Example.com vs name@example.com) incorrectly triggers a mismatch error. Email comparison between these two fields should be case-insensitive so identical addresses differing only by case are accepted without error.
after.title: Go-Checkout Page - Email & Confirm Email Case Sensitivity
verificationCriteria: Given a value typed in the Email field, when the same address is typed into Confirm Email with different letter casing, the rendered checkout form shows no validation error message for the Confirm Email field

Given a value typed in the Email field, when a different address (not just a casing variant) is typed into Confirm Email, the rendered checkout form still shows the existing mismatch error message on the Confirm Email field

notes: Defect in confirmEmail validation on the checkout form: the validate function at src/components/pages/CheckoutPage/CheckoutForm.tsx (around lines 300-306) does a raw `value !== email` comparison, which is case-sensitive. Fix should normalize both values (e.g. lowercase/trim) before comparing, and the same normalization should be applied consistently at submission time so the email sent downstream is not accidentally split by casing.

after.description: On the Go-Checkout page, the Email and Confirm Email fields are compared case-sensitively (CheckoutForm.tsx:306, `value !== email`), so entering the same address with different letter casing (e.g. Name@Example.com vs name@example.com) incorrectly triggers a "TRM774" mismatch error. Comparison must be case-insensitive, and the same normalization must be applied to the value that is actually submitted downstream so a mixed-case email isn't silently altered or mismatched at submit time.
after.title: Go-Checkout Page - Email & Confirm Email Case Sensitivity
verificationCriteria: Given a value typed in the Email field, when the same address is typed into Confirm Email with different letter casing, the rendered checkout form shows no validation error message for the Confirm Email field

Given a value typed in the Email field, when a different address (not just a casing variant) is typed into Confirm Email, the rendered checkout form still shows the existing mismatch error message on the Confirm Email field

notes:
Openspec supplied no acceptanceCriteria (empty array) — I built the full list from the description, technicalNotes, and by reading src/components/pages/CheckoutPage/CheckoutForm.tsx directly (lines ~259-322) to confirm the defect: the `validate` rule on the `confirmEmail` field at line 306 does `value !== email` with no case normalization, and clearErrors on email onChange doesn't re-validate confirmEmail. I traced submission: CheckoutForm calls `handleSubmit(onSubmit)` (line 168) which passes raw, unmodified form values to the parent, confirming that normalization must also apply to the submitted values, not just the inline validator, per openspec's note. I did not find email-handling code in CheckoutPageComponentMapper.tsx or PurchaseConfirmationPageComponentMapper.tsx (grepped, no matches) — those files listed in technicalNotes appear unrelated to this specific validation path; only CheckoutForm.tsx is directly implicated.

Added AC covering: case-insensitive match acceptance, leading/trailing whitespace handling, mismatch still caught for genuinely different addresses, error clears/re-validates when either field changes, no visual alteration of user-typed casing in the input itself, and downstream submission normalization consistency. Flagged one AC (whitespace trimming) since it wasn't explicitly requested by openspec/description and is an assumption about scope. Flagged the "submission normalization" AC as needing product confirmation on exactly what normalized form (lowercase vs as-typed) should be sent downstream, since the story description says "not accidentally split by casing" but doesn't specify the canonical casing to persist.
